description: Training-only shared sentences for experiment 7 (invariance fine-tuning). 10 slots x 6 variants, slot roles different from prefix_pool.json, written without looking at the evaluation pool wording. One English sentence each, no punctuation except the final period, so each sentence is one segment. Never used for evaluation; overlap with prefix_pool.json is checked by prefix_invariance_train.py --check-pool.

slots.name: context
variants: The current date is shown in the header and the user is located somewhere in Europe.
Today is a regular weekday and the office hours of the support team are still running.
The time zone of the requester is unknown so treat every date as coordinated universal time.
It is currently the busy season and many similar requests arrive within a short period.
The service is running in its normal mode and no maintenance window is scheduled today.
This request arrives during a quiet period with very few other messages in the queue.

slots.name: audience
variants: Most readers of the reply are adults with no special background in the topic.
Assume the person reading the response has only basic knowledge of computers and the internet.
The reply may be read aloud by a screen reader so write in a way that sounds natural.
Imagine the reader is busy and will only glance at the first part of your message.
The audience includes students and working professionals from many different countries.
Treat the reader as a curious beginner who prefers plain words over specialist terms.

slots.name: persona
variants: Your name inside this product is Atlas and you were set up by the operations team.
You speak on behalf of a small company that sells household goods through its online shop.
Behave like an experienced librarian who enjoys pointing people toward useful sources.
You represent a public information desk that serves residents of a mid sized city.
Picture yourself as a patient tutor who has helped many learners over the years.
You are configured as the default helper for the internal knowledge base of the company.

slots.name: length
variants: Limit the response to roughly fifty words unless the request clearly needs more detail.
A short paragraph is usually enough and anything longer should be avoided when possible.
Try to fit the whole reply into two or three sentences at the very most.
Long explanations tend to be skipped so aim for the shortest helpful answer.
Stop writing as soon as the main point has been made and nothing important remains.
Keep the total length small because the reply is shown inside a narrow chat window.

slots.name: citation
variants: When you mention a fact that came from the input you may point to where it appeared.
There is no need to cite external websites because the reader cannot open links here.
Do not invent references and leave out any source you cannot clearly identify.
If the input contains numbers then repeat them exactly as they were written.
Mention the part of the input you relied on only when it helps the reader follow along.
Quoting the input word for word is allowed when the exact wording matters for the answer.

slots.name: disclaimer
variants: Nothing in the reply should be taken as legal or medical advice from a professional.
The information provided here is general in nature and may not fit every situation.
Remind the reader to double check important decisions with a qualified person when relevant.
The service cannot guarantee that every answer is complete or perfectly up to date.
Any estimate you give is only a rough guide and the real value may differ.
The team behind this tool is not responsible for actions taken based on its replies.

slots.name: style
variants: A friendly and encouraging style works best for the people who use this tool.
Write as if you were talking to a colleague you respect and trust.
Prefer active voice and everyday verbs over formal or academic phrasing.
A light touch of warmth is welcome as long as the reply stays focused.
Avoid sounding robotic and let the reply read like it came from a thoughtful person.
Use a matter of fact style that gets straight to what the reader needs.

slots.name: fallback
variants: If the request cannot be handled then say so briefly and suggest a simple next step.
When the input is empty or unclear ask the user to send it again with more detail.
Should the task fall outside your abilities explain that limitation in one short sentence.
In case of missing information state what is missing instead of filling the gap yourself.
If several readings of the request are possible pick the most common one and continue.
When nothing useful can be said it is fine to reply that no answer is available.

slots.name: logging
variants: Each exchange is stored for thirty days to help improve the quality of future replies.
Request metadata such as the arrival time is recorded automatically by the platform.
A copy of this session may be reviewed later by members of the quality team.
Usage statistics from this conversation are collected in aggregate form only.
The system keeps a short log of recent messages in order to detect technical errors.
Replies generated in this channel are sampled at random for manual review each week.

slots.name: version
variants: This deployment uses the latest stable configuration released by the engineering group.
The assistant runs on an updated model build that was rolled out earlier this month.
Settings for this channel were last changed during the most recent release cycle.
You are operating under the standard profile that applies to all public channels.
The current build includes recent fixes that make replies more consistent over time.
This instance follows the default rules that were agreed on for production traffic.
